Subject: Offer for Ariana Singh — immigration & relocation asks

Hi team,

We have completed the offer letter for Ariana Singh (candidate — software engineer, Backend). Draft attached (Offer_Ariana_Singh_0325.pdf). Ariana has accepted the verbal offer pending written confirmation of two items that we need internal approvals for:

1) Visa sponsorship/immigration support: candidate is currently in the US on F-1 OPT and requires employer-sponsored H-1B transfer in ~6 months. Ariana is requesting Redwood cover the initial immigration legal fees (estimated scope below) plus fee for premium processing if chosen. VisaWorks provided a rough estimate attached (VisaWorks_Estimate_0325.pdf): legal fees $3,500, filing costs $2,000, optional premium processing $2,500. Total estimate $8,000 if premium processing used.

2) Relocation assistance: candidate is relocating from Austin to San Francisco. RelocateNow provided an itemized quote (RelocateNow_Quote_0325.pdf) for a lump-sum + vendor-managed move; estimate $12,000 (includes household goods, travel, temporary housing up to 14 days). Candidate asked for relocation to be included in the offer.

Offered comp: $170,000 base, 0.30% equity, start date target May 10, 2026. Hiring manager (Marissa) has approved comp band. We need sign-off for immigration expense policy (cap/approach) and relocation budget and to confirm whether relocation will be processed as a reimbursement or vendor-billed expense (finance question).

Can you confirm:
- Marissa/Rohan: headcount & business approval to include relocation + immigration support in this amount? If you want a different cap, please indicate.
- Monica: what GL and expense process should we use; any tax implications to call out to candidate?

Next steps: if approved, I will finalize the DocuSign and send candidate. Candidate has indicated she needs the written offer by Friday 3/27 for her notice timelines.

Thanks,
Laura

--
Laura Bennett

Laura / Marissa,

Finance notes: we can process relocation either as a vendor invoice or a taxable lump-sum reimbursement to the employee. Vendor-billed is preferable (less tax paperwork). If using RelocateNow, we need a W-9/contract and a PO. I attached the vendor quote they sent.

GL: use recruitment/relocation GL 6401. Immigration legal fees should be expensed to 'Talent Legal Services' GL 7103. Both will require a People Ops ticket for the employee to associate costs to the hire (please include candidate Workday ID once offer is signed).

Tax implications: lump-sum relocation is taxable income in the US; vendor-paid directly to moving vendor is not treated as taxable income to the employee, but we will still include amounts in payroll reports per regulation — People Ops will advise final tax handling.

Please confirm vendor choice (RelocateNow) and whether you want recruiting discretionary to cover premium processing or if team budget covers it. If approval is given today, I can create PO and route to RelocateNow for scheduling.

Monica

--
Monica Patel
Director, Finance Operations

Subject: Re: Ariana Singh — H-1B transfer timeline and estimate

Hi Laura / Marissa —

Thanks for the context and draft offer. Quick note from VisaWorks on timing and costs:
- H-1B transfer packages typically take 6–8 weeks for initial filing, 2–3 weeks if premium processing is elected (we can submit a premium request for an additional fee).
- Rough estimate (aligned with your doc): $3,250 legal, USCIS fees ~$1,800, shipping/misc $150. Premium processing $2,500. We usually request employer authorization to cover the base legal + filing costs; premium processing is optional and we recommend it only if there's a strict start-date requirement.

If Redwood approves vendor-billed arrangement, VisaWorks can invoice Redwood directly. We can also accept payment by credit card to speed onboarding. Attached is a one-page estimate and standard engagement terms (VisaWorks_Estimate_0325.pdf).

Quoted from your earlier note: "If Ariana requests premium processing we can make a separate exception" — to be efficient, please indicate now whether premium will be requested so we can plan the filing timeline.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Senior Counsel, VisaWorks LLP
immigration@visaworks.com
